executive_summary.text: Microsoft's June 2026 Patch Tuesday is a record-breaking 206-CVE update that includes three publicly-known zero-days (YellowKey, GreenPlasma, MiniPlasma) disclosed without coordination by researcher Nightmare Eclipse — three of which were exploited before patches landed — plus a fourth Exchange Server zero-day actively exploited in attacks, making this the most consequential Patch Tuesday on record.

The Miasma worm supply chain attack infected 73 Microsoft GitHub repositories — primarily targeting AI coding agents via the Azure Durable Task SDK — and began pushing password-stealing malware to developers before GitHub disabled the compromised repos; Microsoft has partially restored some while the investigation continues.

A zero-day exploit dubbed RoguePlanet exploits a race condition in Microsoft Defender to escalate local privileges to SYSTEM on fully patched Windows systems, and was publicly released by researcher Nightmare Eclipse immediately after Patch Tuesday — meaning exploit code is widely available before widespread patching occurs.

The Check Point Security Gateway IKEv1 authentication bypass (CVE-2026-50751) is being actively weaponized by the Qilin ransomware group to establish unauthorized VPN sessions, earning an emergency CISA KEV due date of June 11 — the shortest remediation window seen this year.

Cisco's Catalyst SD-WAN Manager has now logged its seventh actively exploited zero-day this year (CVE-2026-20245), with no patch or workaround available; simultaneously, Ivanti disclosed a maximum-severity unauthenticated RCE in Sentry and PAN-OS CVE-2026-0257 is under active exploitation — underscoring a systemic crisis in enterprise network appliance security.

cyber_news.title: Miasma Worm Infects 73 Microsoft GitHub Repos in Major Supply Chain Attack
cyber_news.summary: The Miasma worm compromised 73 public Microsoft GitHub repositories, primarily targeting the Azure Durable Task SDK and packages consumed by AI coding agents. GitHub disabled the infected repos after they began distributing password-stealing malware to developers; Microsoft has partially restored some repositories while forensic investigation continues.
cyber_news.expanded: Miasma operated by injecting malicious commit hooks and workflow files into the repository pipeline, enabling it to self-propagate to downstream forks and dependent packages — a wormable supply chain pattern first documented in the Shai Hulud npm worm. The targeting of AI coding agent scaffolding libraries is particularly notable because agentic workflows can auto-fetch and execute code without human review checkpoints. The attack primarily targeted developers and CI/CD pipelines that trust Microsoft-signed packages, meaning credential theft could cascade into enterprise environments. Nightmare Eclipse and the broader researcher community have flagged that AI-accelerated coding pipelines dramatically expand the blast radius of repository-level compromises.

cyber_news.title: Cisco SD-WAN Logs Seventh Zero-Day of 2026 — CVE-2026-20245 — With No Patch Available
cyber_news.summary: CVE-2026-20245, a validation error in Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager, allows authenticated or local attackers to execute arbitrary commands as root. It marks the seventh actively exploited zero-day in Cisco SD-WAN this year; no patch or workaround is currently available and it has been added to the CISA KEV with a June 23 due date.
cyber_news.expanded: The vulnerability stems from improper encoding and escaping of user-supplied input in the SD-WAN Manager's command processing pipeline, allowing crafted file arguments to break out of the intended execution context and run as root. Although exploitation currently requires authentication, the persistence of unpatched Cisco SD-WAN instances across enterprise WAN edges means a single compromised account — obtainable via credential theft or brute force — provides a direct path to full appliance control. The seven-zero-day pattern in a single product family within six months suggests either a systematic architecture flaw being worked by a focused threat group or coordinated vulnerability research targeting a high-value network choke point. CISA's KEV listing obligates federal agencies to remediate by June 23 despite the absence of vendor guidance.

cyber_news.title: RoguePlanet Zero-Day: Public Exploit Grants SYSTEM on Fully Patched Windows via Microsoft Defender Race Condition
cyber_news.summary: Researcher Nightmare Eclipse publicly released a working exploit called RoguePlanet that exploits a race condition in Microsoft Defender to escalate local privileges to SYSTEM on fully updated Windows machines. The exploit dropped immediately after June Patch Tuesday, maximizing the window between exploit availability and enterprise patch deployment.
cyber_news.expanded: The race condition exists in Defender's real-time protection scanning pipeline, where a time-of-check to time-of-use (TOCTOU) flaw can be triggered by a local, unprivileged process to substitute a malicious payload during the scan evaluation window. Because Microsoft Defender runs as SYSTEM and the race window is reliably wideable on modern multi-core hardware, the exploit achieves near-deterministic privilege escalation without requiring kernel exploits. The deliberate post-Patch-Tuesday release timing by Nightmare Eclipse mirrors the YellowKey and GreenPlasma disclosures and appears intended to maximize pressure on Microsoft's disclosure and patch process. Nightmare Eclipse has reportedly threatened a 'bone shattering' July 14 follow-on disclosure, suggesting additional unpatched vulnerabilities are being held.

cyber_news.title: LiteLLM CVE-2026-42271 Command Injection Exploited in the Wild, Chains to Unauthenticated RCE
cyber_news.summary: CVE-2026-42271, a command injection flaw in BerriAI's LiteLLM AI gateway, is being actively exploited and can be chained to achieve unauthenticated remote code execution on host systems. CISA added it to the KEV catalog with a June 22 due date.
cyber_news.expanded: LiteLLM's vulnerability lies in insufficient sanitization of model name or routing parameters passed to shell-invoked processes, allowing injected commands to execute in the context of the LiteLLM server process. The chain to unauthenticated RCE exploits the fact that LiteLLM's proxy API accepts certain configuration-altering requests before authentication state is enforced — effectively turning any network-reachable LiteLLM instance into an unauthenticated remote execution surface. The severity is amplified by LiteLLM's role as a centralized AI gateway: a compromise grants access to API keys for multiple LLM providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Azure OpenAI) stored in the platform, enabling credential theft at scale. This represents the first major exploitation of an AI orchestration layer in the wild and signals that AI infrastructure is becoming a primary attack surface.

cyber_news.title: PAN-OS CVE-2026-0257 Authentication Bypass Under Active Exploitation
cyber_news.summary: Unit 42 has documented active exploitation of CVE-2026-0257, an authentication bypass in PAN-OS that allows attackers to bypass security restrictions and establish unauthorized VPN connections. The vulnerability affects Palo Alto Networks firewalls and secure access gateways.
cyber_news.expanded: CVE-2026-0257 abuses a flaw in PAN-OS's IKE/VPN authentication state machine, where a specially crafted IKE packet sequence can convince the gateway to advance to an authenticated state without valid credentials being presented — similar in class to the Check Point IKEv1 flaw disclosed this week. Exploitation allows adversaries to establish fully-tunneled VPN sessions that appear legitimate in log telemetry, enabling stealthy lateral movement or data exfiltration through what defenders treat as trusted network paths. The simultaneous exploitation of authentication bypass vulnerabilities in both Check Point and PAN-OS VPN products suggests active threat actor interest in this vulnerability class, possibly coordinated reconnaissance across enterprise VPN gateway vendors. Unit 42 has published indicators and mitigation steps in its threat brief.

cyber_news.title: Hades PyPI Attack and Proto6 Vulnerabilities: Dual Supply Chain Threats Hit Developer Ecosystems
cyber_news.summary: Two simultaneous supply chain threats emerged this week: the 'Hades' campaign poisoned 19 PyPI packages to auto-execute a Bun-based credential stealer on installation, while six 'Proto6' vulnerabilities in protobuf.js expose Node.js applications to RCE and DoS. Together they represent sustained, multi-ecosystem targeting of developer infrastructure.
cyber_news.expanded: The Hades PyPI attack used typosquatting and dependency confusion techniques to insert packages that execute a post-install script invoking Bun — a fast JavaScript runtime — to run an in-memory credential harvester that targets browser-stored credentials, cloud CLI tokens, and SSH keys. The Proto6 vulnerabilities in protobuf.js are distinct: they include prototype pollution, type confusion, and integer overflow flaws exploitable during deserialization of untrusted protobuf payloads, making any Node.js service that processes external protobuf data a potential RCE target. Both attacks underscore that supply chain targeting has matured beyond single-vector attacks into coordinated multi-ecosystem campaigns designed to maximize developer environment coverage. The Red Hat npm scope backdoor (32 packages stealing CI/CD secrets) reported earlier this week reinforces the same pattern.

cyber_news.title: CISA Shifts to Risk-Based Vulnerability Prioritization with New Binding Operational Directive
cyber_news.summary: CISA acting director Nick Andersen announced a forthcoming binding operational directive that moves federal agencies away from blanket fast-patching guidance toward risk-based, asset-specific prioritization aligned with the KEV catalog and internet-exposed asset posture.
cyber_news.expanded: The new framework explicitly acknowledges that 'patch everything within 15 days' mandates have created compliance theater at the expense of genuine risk reduction. The directive will tier remediation timelines based on asset internet exposure, known exploitation status (KEV alignment), and asset criticality classification. For the private sector, CISA plans accompanying guidance rather than binding mandates.

cyber_news.title: Threat Actors Weaponize AI Brand Impersonation in Phishing and Malvertising Campaigns
cyber_news.summary: Microsoft Threat Intelligence documented campaigns impersonating ChatGPT, Claude, DeepSeek, and Copilot brands through phishing, malvertising, and SEO poisoning to deliver Vidar Stealer and credential harvesters. Initial access broker Storm-3075 and malware-signing service Fox Tempest are linked to multiple campaigns.
cyber_news.expanded: The campaigns exploit high user trust in AI brand names and the expectation of downloading new AI tools or extensions, lowering the psychological barrier to execution of malicious payloads. Attackers are using Google Ads and SEO manipulation to surface malicious download pages above legitimate AI vendor sites. Fox Tempest provides adversaries with Authenticode-signed binaries that bypass SmartScreen and endpoint reputation checks, giving Vidar Stealer a clean initial execution path.

cyber_news.title: Unit 42: Threat Actors Abusing Cloud Logging Services to Blind Defenders
cyber_news.summary: Unit 42 research details attack scenarios in which threat actors manipulate or suppress cloud logging pipelines — including AWS CloudTrail, Azure Monitor, and GCP Cloud Logging — to achieve defense evasion and eliminate forensic visibility during intrusions.
cyber_news.expanded: Attacker techniques include using legitimate IAM permissions to disable log delivery, modifying log filter exclusions to suppress high-signal event categories, and leveraging cloud-native event bridge features to redirect logs to attacker-controlled sinks. Unit 42's mitigations focus on immutable log archiving to separate accounts, alerting on log configuration changes, and enforcing SCPs that prevent log disablement.

cyber_news.title: Nightmare Eclipse Controversy Reignites Coordinated Vulnerability Disclosure Debate After Microsoft Zero-Days Exploited Pre-Patch
cyber_news.summary: The uncoordinated public disclosure of multiple Windows zero-days by researcher Nightmare Eclipse — three of which were exploited before patches were available — has sparked a major industry debate about disclosure ethics, vendor accountability, and the limits of coordinated vulnerability disclosure frameworks. Microsoft has threatened legal action.
cyber_news.expanded: Nightmare Eclipse disclosed YellowKey, GreenPlasma, MiniPlasma, and RoguePlanet without notifying Microsoft, arguing that vendors exploit long disclosure windows to delay patching. Microsoft's counter-position is that uncoordinated disclosure created a weaponizable window that threat actors exploited. The researcher's threat of a 'bone shattering' July 14 disclosure suggests the pressure campaign is ongoing.

deep_dive.title: Microsoft June 2026 Patch Tuesday: Record 206 CVEs, Three Pre-Exploited Zero-Days, and the Nightmare Eclipse Disclosure Crisis
deep_dive.content: Microsoft's June 2026 Patch Tuesday is the largest single monthly patch release on record, addressing 206 CVEs including 32 critical remote code execution flaws across RDP, Hyper-V, the Windows Kernel, HTTP Stack, Outlook, and Word. The update includes patches for three publicly known zero-days — YellowKey, GreenPlasma, and MiniPlasma — all disclosed without coordination by researcher Nightmare Eclipse, plus a separately exploited Exchange Server zero-day. Talos identified CVE-2026-42985 (RDP RCE) and CVE-2026-47291 (HTTP Stack integer overflow) as the critical flaws most likely to see near-term exploitation. The volume surge is partly attributed to AI-assisted vulnerability discovery tooling — both by Microsoft internally and by researchers — dramatically accelerating the identification of previously overlooked flaws. Complicating the patch cycle, Nightmare Eclipse released a working RoguePlanet exploit for the Defender race condition the same day patches dropped, and has threatened further disclosures on July 14. An OpenAI Codex-reported Windows Defender flaw was also included, marking the first time an AI coding assistant has been credited in a major Patch Tuesday advisory. Google simultaneously patched 429 Chrome CVEs in the same week, creating an unprecedented enterprise patch management burden.

biggest_hacks.title: Miasma Worm Compromises 73 Microsoft GitHub Repositories in Supply Chain Attack Targeting AI Agents
biggest_hacks.summary: A self-propagating worm infected 73 public Microsoft GitHub repos and used them to distribute password-stealing malware to developers before GitHub disabled the repositories.

biggest_hacks.title: ServiceNow Vulnerability Exploited Against Customer Instances — Company Had Knowledge Since April 7
biggest_hacks.summary: A ServiceNow security vulnerability was actively exploited to gain unauthorized access to customer instances; the company was aware since April 7 before deploying a fix.

biggest_hacks.title: Meta AI Support Bot Exploited to Hijack 20,000+ Instagram Accounts
biggest_hacks.summary: Pro-Iran hackers exploited a flaw in Meta's AI customer support chatbot to bypass email verification during password resets and hijack Instagram accounts at scale.

biggest_hacks.title: Red Hat npm Scope Backdoored: 32 Packages Steal Cloud Secrets from CI/CD Pipelines
biggest_hacks.summary: Attackers backdoored 32 packages in Red Hat's official npm scope to exfiltrate cloud credentials and CI/CD pipeline secrets.

biggest_hacks.title: Check Point VPN CVE-2026-50751 Exploited by Qilin Ransomware to Bypass Authentication
biggest_hacks.summary: Qilin ransomware is actively exploiting CVE-2026-50751 in Check Point Security Gateways to bypass IKEv1 VPN authentication, earning CISA's shortest remediation window of 2026.

vulnerabilities.description: Improper authentication in IKEv1 implementation allows unauthenticated remote attackers to establish VPN sessions without valid credentials. Actively exploited by Qilin ransomware group. Emergency CISA KEV due date: 2026-06-11.

vulnerabilities.description: Deserialization of untrusted PHP object enables unauthenticated RCE. Actively exploited. CISA KEV due date: 2026-06-06 (passed).
